The report follows: # Pagy upgrade plan for Margin Notes: 8.6.3 to 9.3.5 The skill asked me to hand this to the `maintain-rails:gem-upgrade-planner` agent. No subagent tool was available in this session, so I did the planning myself using that agent's brief. The working repo at `/home/user/workspace/repo` is unchanged (HEAD `9938031`, clean). All experiments ran in disposable clones with their own Postgres and Redis. ## Verdict The upgrade is small but needs three code changes at the moment of the bump, and one of them fixes a behavior change that pagy's changelog doesn't flag as breaking: 1. **Boot fails as-is.** The initializer requires `pagy/extras/items`, which no longer exists in 9.x, so the app won't start. 2. **Settings and the view must be renamed.** The `items` settings and the `@pagy.items` call in the notes list are gone in 9.x. 3. **Invalid page numbers now crash the notes list.** In 8.6.3, pagy itself turned a blank, `0`, negative or non-numeric `page` into page 1. In 9.3.5 these raise `Pagy::VariableError`, which is a 500 error. `ARCHITECTURE.md` documents the page-1 behavior. The existing tests catch all three. The silent risk is a careless rename. If the old `items` settings are left in place, the app still boots but quietly ignores them: 20 notes per page, `per_page` ignored, no 50 cap, and a new `limit=` parameter added to every link. ## Where the app uses pagy | Location | What it uses | |---|---| | `Gemfile:32`, `Gemfile.lock:178,301` | `gem "pagy", "8.6.3"` | | `config/initializers/pagy.rb` | `require "pagy/extras/items"` and `"pagy/extras/overflow"`; settings `items: 10`, `items_param: :per_page`, `max_items: 50`, `overflow: :last_page` | | `app/controllers/notes_controller.rb:2,18` | `include Pagy::Backend`; `@pagy, @notes = pagy(@notes)` | | `app/helpers/application_helper.rb:2` | `include Pagy::Frontend` | | `app/views/notes/index.html.erb` | `@pagy.items` (line 30), `pagy_info(... item_name:)` (line 40), `@pagy.pages`, `@pagy.prev`, `@pagy.next`, `pagy_url_for` (lines 59–62) | | `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css:86-87` | Styles the app's own `.pagination` and `[rel=next]`, not pagy's classes | | `test/controllers/notes_controller_test.rb` | "pages through filtered notes…" and "invalid pages show the first page…" | | Docs | `ARCHITECTURE.md:17-23` and `docs/guides/controllers.md:108` say "Pagy 8.6.3" | Things that aren't used, checked by grep: pagy JavaScript or CSS (nothing in the importmap, `app/javascript`, `vendor` or `public`), custom pagy translations, `pagy_nav` and the other nav helpers, pagy in jobs or mailers, and caching of the notes list. ## Required changes ### R1. Initializer: rename the extra and the settings (same commit as the bump) - **Affected code:** `config/initializers/pagy.rb`. - **Applies because:** 9.3.5 ships no `lib/pagy/extras/items.rb`. Variant A failed with `LoadError: cannot load such file -- pagy/extras/items` in `db:prepare`, `zeitwerk:check` and the test run. - **Recommendation:** use the upstream rename table (CHANGELOG, "Version 9.0.0"). ```ruby require "pagy/extras/limit" require "pagy/extras/overflow" Pagy::DEFAULT[:limit] = 10 Pagy::DEFAULT[:limit_param] = :per_page # keep the existing URL parameter Pagy::DEFAULT[:limit_max] = 50 Pagy::DEFAULT[:overflow] = :last_page ``` Keep `limit_param = :per_page`. Without it the parameter becomes `limit`, and existing bookmarks and links with `per_page=` silently fall back to the default page size. - **Works on 8.6.3?** No. 8.6.3 has no `extras/limit.rb` (source), so this can't land before the bump. - **Validation:** the app boots, and `Pagy::DEFAULT` contains `limit: 10, limit_param: :per_page, limit_max: 50` with no `items*` keys (probe dump in `probe-v9-C.json`). - The tests that tell a correct rename from a sloppy one are the existing "pages through…" test (5 per page, `per_page` in the links) and the cap at 50. - Variant A2b (old setting names left in place) boots but fails 2 of those tests: 20 per page, `per_page=500` not capped, links gain `&limit=20`. ### R2. Make invalid page numbers show page 1 again (can land first, on 8.6.3) - **Affected code:** `NotesController#index`, line 18. - **Applies because:** - 8.6.3's `pagy_get_page` clamps the value: `[params[...].to_i, 1].max`. - 9.0.0 returns the raw parameter, and 9.0.3+ returns `(page || 1).to_i`. - In 9.3.5, `""`, `"0"`, `"-1"` and `"two"` all become a number below 1 and raise `Pagy::VariableError: expected :page >= 1` (variant B). - The upstream CHANGELOG lists this only as "Improve pagy_get_page with force_integer option", not as a breaking change. - **Recommendation:** pass the page explicitly, which is the documented way to pass options and works on both versions: ```ruby @pagy, @notes = pagy(@notes, page: [params[:page].to_i, 1].max) ``` The patch is at `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/scripts/page-normalization.patch`. It reproduces 8.6.3's arithmetic exactly. A `page[]=` array parameter still raises `NoMethodError`, as it does today. - **Works on 8.6.3?** Yes, executed: - Variant D (8.6.3 plus this change) passes 46/46 tests. - All 20 probe cases match the 8.6.3 baseline exactly. - Shipping it first lets every running process behave identically before and after the bump. - **Validation:** the existing test "invalid pages show the first page and page size is capped at 50" fails without R2 on 9.3.5 (variant B) and passes with it (variant C). ### R3. View: `@pagy.items` becomes `@pagy.limit` (same commit as the bump) - **Affected code:** `app/views/notes/index.html.erb:30`. - **Applies because:** in 9.3.5 the shared reader methods are `page`, `limit` and `vars`, and `items` is gone. Variant A2 raised `ActionView::Template::Error: undefined method 'items'` on every request to the notes list. - **Recommendation:** change it to `@pagy.limit`. - **Works on 8.6.3?** No. 8.6.3 has no `limit` reader (source). - A version-neutral alternative would be `@notes.limit_value`. I did not test it, and I don't think it's worth coupling the view to the query just to save one line. - **Validation:** the existing test asserts `select[name=per_page] option[selected]` is "5". The probe also confirmed the selected option for 5, 10 and 50, and that 7 has no selected option, the same as on 8.6.3. ### R4. Gemfile, lockfile and docs - **Gemfile:** `gem "pagy", "9.3.5"`, keeping the repo's exact-pin convention. - **Lockfile:** `bundle lock --update pagy --conservative` changed only the two pagy lines (`git diff` in variant A). Pagy has no runtime dependencies. It requires Ruby 3.1 or later; the app uses 3.3.6. - **Docs:** update `ARCHITECTURE.md:17` and `docs/guides/controllers.md:108` from "Pagy 8.6.3" to "Pagy 9.3.5". Note that the app now normalizes `page` itself, and that the initializer sets the limit settings. `ARCHITECTURE.md:23` ("Pagy raises `Pagy::VariableError`" for a bad `per_page`) is still true. ## Unchanged behavior (verified by the variant C probe against the 8.6.3 baseline) - **Links:** `href` values are identical, including parameter order: `page`, `per_page`, the filters, and the `/journal` path. - **Overflow:** a page past the end, such as `page=6` or `page=99999999999999999999`, shows the last page. - **Page parsing:** `"1.5"` gives page 1 and `"2abc"` gives page 2. - **Ignored parameters:** `limit=5` and `items=5` are ignored when the parameter is `per_page`. - **`pagy_info` markup:** identical: `Displaying notes 1-10 of 52 in total`. The `pagy.info.*` keys in the English locale are unchanged; only `items_selector_js` was renamed, and the app doesn't use it. - **Invalid `per_page`** (`""`, `"0"`, `"-3"`, `"abc"`): still raises `Pagy::VariableError`, but the message changes from `expected :items >= 1` to `expected :limit >= 1`, and `#variable` changes from `:items` to `:limit`. - This isn't covered by tests. It matters only if error tracking or log alerts match on that text. ## Optional (not required) - **`Pagy::DEFAULT.freeze` at the end of the initializer**, as the 9.3.5 config template recommends. Variant E passes 46/46 with a probe identical to C. It must come after all `require "pagy/extras/..."` lines, because extras write to `DEFAULT` when loaded. - **Upstream's suggested `~> 9.3` constraint.** I'd leave it out because CLAUDE.md asks to keep the exact pins. - **Switching the parameter to the default `limit`: not recommended.** It breaks bookmarked and shared `per_page=` URLs and complicates rollback. - **Handling invalid `per_page` gracefully.** This is a behavior change outside the upgrade's scope. - **Not affected:** the 9.0 removals of the `foundation`, `materialize`, `semantic` and `uikit` styles, the `pagy.js` renames, array `:size`, `:anchor_string` and `:fragment`. The app uses none of them. ## Rollout, rollback and running two versions at once - **Order:** 1. Deploy R2 alone on 8.6.3. It's verified to change nothing. 2. Deploy R1, R3 and R4 together. 3. Docs go with step 2. - **Old and new processes side by side:** both versions generate identical links and identical page parameters, so a link rendered by one works on the other. Pagy only ever generates valid page numbers, so the R2 gap would only show up for hand-edited, bookmarked or crawled URLs. Shipping R2 first closes it for every process. - **Rollback:** revert R1, R3 and R4 together and keep R2. A partial revert breaks boot (8.6.3 with `require "pagy/extras/limit"` raises `LoadError`; this is from the source, not executed). Because the URL parameter stays `per_page`, URLs created after the upgrade still work after a rollback. - **Stored data:** none. Pagy keeps no state in the database, session (which holds only `user_id`) or cookies. - **Caches:** - Nothing caches pagination markup: the notes list has no fragment caching or `fresh_when`/`stale?`, and the only `cache` block is in `exports/_export.html.erb`. - Turbo Drive's client-side page snapshots hold markup that is structurally identical in both versions. - **Queued work:** the five Sidekiq jobs don't reference pagy and their arguments contain no pagy objects (grep), so nothing needs draining. ## Executed checks All of these ran under `/tmp/pagy-upgrade`. **Isolation** - **Postgres:** a private cluster on socket `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/services/pg`, port 55439. Each clone's `database.yml` was edited to point there, with databases named `margin_notes_pagy_{v8,v9}_test`. `DATABASE_URL` was unset. I checked afterwards that no pagy databases exist on the shared server. - **Redis:** a private instance on 127.0.0.1:56379 with saving off, used via `REDIS_URL`. This matters because `User#request_digest` calls `Sidekiq.redis` directly, even in tests. The `digest_requests:*` keys appeared only in the private instance. - **Cache and storage:** the test environment uses `null_store`, and storage goes to `tmp/storage` inside each clone. - **Ruby, gems and tools:** - Ruby: `/home/user/.local/share/mise/installs/ruby/3.3.6/bin` was put first on PATH, so I didn't need to `mise trust` the clones. - pagy 9.3.5: installed into its own `GEM_HOME=/tmp/pagy-upgrade/gems-v9`. Its SHA256 `78a95131…0fd7` matches rubygems.org. - Bundler: `BUNDLE_APP_CONFIG` was set per variant. - All environment settings are in `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/env.sh`. - **Both services are now stopped.** **Clones and variants** The clones are `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/app-v8` and `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/app-v9`, each with the isolation commit on top of `9938031`. Each variant ran `bin/rails db:prepare`, `zeitwerk:check`, `bin/rails test`, and then the probe. The probe is `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/scripts/pagy_probe_test.rb`; it was copied in temporarily and writes `logs/probe-.json`. | Variant | Commit | pagy | Tests | Log | |---|---|---|---|---| | v8 baseline | 1808919 | 8.6.3 | 46 runs / 325 assertions, 0 failures | `logs/v8-baseline-test.log`, `probe-v8-baseline.json` | | v8-D (R2 only) | edb4e38 | 8.6.3 | 46/325 pass; probe identical to baseline | `logs/v8-D-test.log`, `probe-v8-D.json` | | v9-A (Gemfile bump only) | 5a735ec | 9.3.5 | `LoadError: pagy/extras/items` at boot | `logs/v9-A-test.log`, `logs/v9-bundle.log` | | v9-A2 (extra renamed, old setting names, view unchanged) | 63b8177 | 9.3.5 | Errors: `undefined method 'items'` | `logs/v9-A2-test.log`, `probe-v9-A2.json` | | v9-A2b (A2 plus view fix) | 19e9c22 | 9.3.5 | 2 failures; 20 per page, `per_page` ignored, `limit=20` in links | `logs/v9-A2b-test.log`, `probe-v9-A2b.json` | | v9-B (R1 + R3) | 473efa4 | 9.3.5 | 1 error: `VariableError: expected :page >= 1; got 0` | `logs/v9-B-test.log`, `probe-v9-B.json` | | v9-C (R1 + R2 + R3) | 402c227 | 9.3.5 | 46/325 pass; probe matches baseline except `per_page` error text | `logs/v9-C-test.log`, `probe-v9-C.json` | | v9-E (C plus `DEFAULT.freeze`) | 5cfe180 | 9.3.5 | 46/325 pass; probe identical to C | `logs/v9-E-test.log`, `probe-v9-E.json` | The suite ran serially: 46 tests is below Rails' parallel threshold of 50, so only one test database was used. **Sources compared:** 8.6.3 (copied from the installed gem) and 9.3.5 (unpacked), both under `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/src/`. I also looked at `backend.rb` from 9.0.0 and 9.0.3 to date the page-parsing change. The upstream changelog for 9.3.5 is at `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/docs/CHANGELOG.md`. ## Checks still to do - **Before deploying:** - Check whether error tracking or log alerts match on `expected :items >= 1`. - Confirm whether production deploys are rolling or all-at-once. - Confirm the production cache store. It isn't configured in the repo, but this upgrade doesn't touch caching. - **On staging, after deploying:** - Open `/notes` and `/journal` with old bookmarked URLs: `?per_page=25&page=3`, `?page=0`, `?page=999`. - Confirm the page-size selector and the "Displaying notes…" text. - **Browser tests:** `bin/rails test:system` has nothing to run because `test/system/` is empty, so browser behavior is covered only by the request-level probe. ## Not verified, and open questions - **Version-neutral view alternative:** `@notes.limit_value` was not tested. - **The reverse partial rollback** (8.6.3 with the 9.x initializer) is from the source only, not executed. - **Newer versions:** pagy 9.4.0 (2025-08-13) and 43.x exist. I didn't review them, because 9.3.5 was requested exactly. - **Outside users of the URLs:** does anything outside this repo build `/notes` URLs with `items=` or `limit=`? 9938031 Load the local maintenance plugin during orb setup
# Readers choose a page size through the per_page URL parameter, capped at 50.
require "pagy/extras/items"
# A page past the end, such as a stale bookmark, shows the last page instead of failing.
require "pagy/extras/overflow"

Pagy::DEFAULT[:items] = 10
Pagy::DEFAULT[:items_param] = :per_page
Pagy::DEFAULT[:max_items] = 50
Pagy::DEFAULT[:overflow] = :last_page
    @notes = @notes.where(status: params[:status]) if Note.statuses.key?(params[:status])
    @notes = @notes.titled_like(params[:query]) if params[:query].present?

    @pagy, @notes = pagy(@notes)
  end

    <%= form.select :per_page, options_for_select([5, 10, 25, 50], @pagy.items) %>
page-normalization.patch
pagy_probe_test.rb
